lenses.title: Door policies
lenses.intro: Each policy estimates how a public detector could read your essay, using that tool’s published descriptions. Open one to see why it might disagree.
lenses.old: Lens estimates are unavailable for this saved result.
lenses.disclaimer: An approximation of publicly described behavior. The real {vendor} model is proprietary; not affiliated or endorsed.
lenses.quick: This policy needs Deep sentence scores.
lenses.note: Policies approximate publicly described behavior. The real tools are proprietary; vibechecker is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.
lenses.zerogptGist: A loose threshold that flags more human essays.
lenses.veriguideGist: Lowest confidence, with little public detail.
lenses.qual: Qualitative only. No published numerical target.
lenses.measure: Held-out high flags: {hits} of {n}. Lens target: {target}.
lenses.denominator: Turnitin’s published 4% uses all highlighted sentences as its denominator. On the mixed-genre check, people wrote {hits} of the {n} highlighted sentences ({share}).
lenses.essayAudit: For the essay-specific calibration, we reserved {docs} human essays for validation. The lens flagged {hits} of their {n} sentences ({rate}).
lenses.broadAudit: At the cutoff used in the app, the lens flagged {hits} of {n} human sentences ({rate}) in a separate check covering several genres.
lenses.broadMiss: The mixed-genre check fell outside the planned tolerance.
lenses.turnitin: Mixed authorship makes sentence boundaries unreliable. Shares from 1% to 19% are masked.
lenses.gptzero: Predictability and sentence variation carry extra weight. The reference rate comes from the vendor’s TOEFL study. Our comparison uses longer second-language essays.
lenses.zerogpt: A loose threshold can flag roughly one in five human essays in the reference benchmark.
lenses.grammarly: Uniform sentence lengths and polished prose can raise this lens for a human writer.
lenses.veriguide: Lowest confidence. This lens compares a short list of common phrases and the encoder signal. Public detail is limited.

kit.heading: Bring your own proof
kit.process: What to bring to a conversation
kit.advice: Gather your outline, dated drafts, reading notes and revision history. Explain one change you made and why. These records give the score context.
kit.why: The index combines patterns in English writing. Predictable phrasing, careful editing and second-language writing can all influence the result.
kit.limits: The likely range describes uncertainty in the index. A score cannot establish who wrote the essay.

policy.data: When you submit English text, VibeChecker sends it to our inference service for scoring. Your browser keeps the essay, result and claim token for up to 30 days and clears expired entries when you return. Use “Forget on this device” to remove them sooner.
policy.features: We keep numerical writing signals separately, without essay text or account IDs, to evaluate the detector. They expire from the database after seven days. Archived signals in Cloudflare R2 expire after 12 months.
policy.purpose: We use your email and account ID for sign-in and history. We store scores, signal values, offsets and an estimated word count for 30 days. Signed-in writers may explicitly save a separately encrypted essay for the same period. Device and network identifiers are keyed hashes used for daily limits. Quota records expire after seven days.
policy.transfers: Vercel runs the web app and Supabase stores account data in Singapore. Cloudflare verifies requests. Our Mac inference service or Modal processes the submitted essay in memory. Resend can deliver sign-in email and Google handles Google sign-in if you choose it. These providers and Sentry may process service data in the United States. Sentry receives limited error categories.
policy.rightsTitle: Your choices under Hong Kong’s PDPO
policy.rights: You can use the checker without an account. History lets you read and delete one check, all checks or your account. To request access to or correction of your personal data, or ask about handling and transfers, contact hello@vibechecker.io. Encrypted backups, where enabled, expire within 14 days.
policy.use: Use this free research beta to understand writing you have the right to submit. Keep other people’s personal or confidential information out of your submission.
policy.limits: A detector score is a reason to look closer, never proof. Discuss the writing process with the author. Automated accusation pipelines, disciplinary decisions based only on a score, and attempts to bypass usage limits are prohibited.
policy.beta: The service is for non-commercial use. Model coverage and calibration are limited. Lenses approximate public descriptions and can disagree with the proprietary tools. Contact hello@vibechecker.io with questions.

home.title:
Does your essay

give robot vibes?
home.subline: Paste it in. We’ll show you what detectors notice at the door, and why they’re often wrong.
home.quotaNote: Resets at midnight in Hong Kong.
home.sampleQuick: A Quick check gets a hand stamp. A riso flyer with your robot vibes, the likely range and the door policies that read your essay.
home.sampleDeep: A Deep check gets the guest pass. Every sentence goes under the UV light, with all eight signals and five door policies.
home.step1Body: No one is turned away. A check shows which patterns a detector might notice, with an honest range around the score.
home.step2Body: Five door policies estimate how different public detectors could read the same essay, and why they disagree.
home.step3Body: Drafts, notes and revision history explain your process better than any score. The evidence kit helps you gather them.

result.title: Robot vibes
result.swing: Drag the pass to swing it
result.passNotProof: Vibe checked · not proof of authorship
result.upsellBody: A Deep check reads every sentence under the UV light, adds four more signals and unlocks the Turnitin-style policy. It takes 300–2,500 words.
result.signalsIntro: Each stub compares your essay with the median human essay the detector learned from. One signal has many possible explanations.

interpretation.low: Your writing shares fewer of the patterns our detector associates with AI-generated text.
interpretation.mixed: Some patterns resemble human writing and others resemble machine-generated text.
interpretation.high: Several patterns resemble machine-generated text. A human writer can produce these patterns too.

result.whyBody: The index combines the signals below and calibrates them against human and AI writing with a 50% prior. Each signal compares your essay with the median human training essay. A single signal has many possible explanations.
result.wrongBody: Short, polished or formulaic passages can look predictable. People writing in a second language may be flagged more often. The range shows uncertainty in calibration. It cannot establish who wrote an essay. Keep drafts, notes and revision history as evidence of your process.
result.invisible: The text contains invisible formatting characters, which can affect how words are read.
result.homoglyph: Some characters look like letters from another script. Check whether they were intentional.
result.saved: This browser keeps your essay and claim token for 30 days.

e1.title: Predictability
e1.detail: Like guessing the next word in a sentence. Lower perplexity means the language model found the wording easier to anticipate.

e2.title: Word choices
e2.detail: Like checking how far down a list of suggestions each word appears. Lower log-rank means more top-ranked words.

e6.title: Learned patterns
e6.detail: A classifier compares short passages with patterns it learned from labelled examples. A higher value means a closer match to its AI-labelled examples.

stylometry.title: Vocabulary variety
stylometry.detail: The share of distinct words in the essay. Topic, word count and a writer’s vocabulary can all change this ratio.

result.esl: Some patterns here also occur in second-language English writing. Detectors can over-flag this writing, so read the index with extra caution and keep your drafts.
result.laundering: Some patterns resemble text that has been reformatted or rewritten. Editing and translation can produce similar patterns.

e3.title: Word likelihood gap
e3.detail: Two language models estimate how likely a typical next word would be. Fast-DetectGPT compares the words actually used with that expectation.

e4.title: Model agreement
e4.detail: Binoculars compares how surprising the essay is to one model with how much two related models disagree about possible next words.

e5.title: Sentence patterns
e5.detail: A sentence model looks at how word predictability changes within each sentence. The map shows where it found stronger and weaker patterns.

e7.title: Patterns across models
e7.detail: A classifier compares patterns in the word-level signals across the essay with those in its training examples.

method.intro: How we measure the detector’s mistakes, interpret its index and check whether its results hold up across different groups of writers.
method.auditBody: The audit reserved {reserved, number} documents from separate source groups before scoring. Of these, {scored, number} met the input requirements for {version}.
method.reliabilityBody: Each point groups essays with similar scores. Its horizontal position is the mean predicted score and its height is the observed share of AI essays. Points on the diagonal agree with the observations.
method.noBins: The Deep report has no held-out calibration measurements yet.
method.fprBody: Among human essays in each group, this is the share that received a high index. The 95% Wilson interval reflects uncertainty from the sample size.
method.cohortNote: The US comparison group comes from the Hewlett dataset. Individual native-language status is unverified. TOEFL estimates require essays that pass the mode’s English and length checks.
method.priorBody: The index is calibrated to a population where {prior}% of essays are AI-written. The mix in a classroom can be very different. A high index alone cannot establish authorship.
method.example: For example, suppose a detector flags 80% of AI essays and 2% of human essays in a group of 1,000. These rates illustrate the calculation.
method.aiShare: Share of AI essays in the group
method.exampleResult: It would flag {aiFlags, number} AI essays and {humanFlags, number} human essays. Of all the essays flagged, {share} would be AI-written.
method.toeflSkipped: The length check excluded {n, plural, one {# TOEFL essay} other {# TOEFL essays}} from this evaluation.
